cards.front: Recall a key point about Minimalist Music
cards.back: Minimalism uses repetitive patterns that change GRADUALLY — tiny alterations accumulate into significant musical transformation over time.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minimalist Music
cards.back: Reich's phase shifting involves identical patterns starting together then gradually moving out of sync — creating complex textures from simple material.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minimalist Music
cards.back: Minimalist harmony often centres on a single chord or slow-moving progression — harmonic stasis focuses attention on rhythm, texture and timbre.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minimalist Music
cards.back: Technology enabled minimalist techniques: Reich's tape loops, Riley's keyboard delays, Adams' digital processing all expand what is possible with repetition.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Name minimalist techniques (phase shifting, layering, additive process). Explain HOW patterns change, not just that they repeat. Identify technology's role. Analyse texture and rhythm.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Minimalist music is just the same thing repeated over and over. Correct: Minimalist repetition is a COMPOSITIONAL STRATEGY — the interest lies in how patterns GRADUALLY TRANSFORM through addition, subtraction, phase shifting and layering. cards.front: Applying Minimalist Music in Performance and Composition
cards.back: Understanding minimalist music informs your performing (AO1) and composing (AO2) work. In performance, awareness of minimalist music helps you make interpretive decisions that serve the music. In composition, minimalist music provides the building blocks of your creative work — the choices you make about this element shape the identity and coherence of your piece.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Minimalist Music Questions
cards.back: In the AQA GCSE Music listening exam, questions about minimalist music typically ask you to: identify features by ear; describe how they are used; explain their effect; compare features between extracts. The key to success is precise terminology — never use vague language.
